context.guidance: Require authentication on every route that returns Personal Data, and check on each request that the authenticated Data Principal owns the record or holds a role authorised for it. Do not let an identifier supplied in the path or body decide ownership. Apply the check to every method on the route, because Rule 6(1)(b) requires access to the resources holding Personal Data to be controlled.

value.fix: Do not look up orders by an email supplied in the request. Take the Data Principal from the authenticated session (for example `req.user.id`), and query with that identity: `db.ordersCollection.find({ userId: req.user.id })` or `find({ email: req.user.email })`, using the verified session email rather than `updatedEmail`. If the caller may legitimately view another user's orders, allow it only when `req.user.role` is authorised for that resource, and check that role on every request. Require authentication on the route and enforce the same ownership or role check on every HTTP method that touches these orders, including GET, PUT/PATCH, and DELETE, so Rule 6(1)(b) access control covers all resources holding Personal Data. Return 401 for unauthenticated requests and 403 (or 404) when the record isn't owned by the caller and the caller lacks an authorised role. Add tests that confirm a user cannot read or change another user's orders by changing the email or ID in the path or body.
